newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania to draw up plan for telecom sale.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania to draw up plan for telecom sale.

text.p: Lithuania's Ministry for European Affairs said on Wednesday it is to help draw up a programme to privatise state-owned Lithuanian Telecom and pledged to offer a privatisation programme for one state company a month.
Lithuania's new right-wing government has vowed to speed privatisation and attract more foreign investors. It aims to sell firms previously considered strategic and banned from sale.

"The prime minister empowered the European Affairs ministry, the privatisation agency and privatisation commission to declare an international bid to draw up a privatisation programme for Lithuanian Telecom," the ministry said in a statement.
A spokesman for the finance ministry said the programme for Lithuanian Telecom's sale would be ready in March.
"Until the end of the year, bids will be declared every month for other companies on the (privatisation) list," the European Affairs ministry added.
The ministry also said it was preparing a programme aimed at making the country more friendly to foreign investors.
"The government has decided to take decisive steps and declared that the encouragement of direct investments is one of its main priorities," the ministry said.
It said a programme to encourage foreign direct investment would be drawn up and presented to parliament no later than May.
The ministry said the programme would focus attention on a number of key areas, including legal, tax and customs reform.
It also said it planned to merge the Lithuanian Investment Agency with the Lithuanian Export Development Agency.
Lithuania has failed to attract the same levels of foreign investment that have poured into its Baltic neighbours and is keen on changing its image as a regional laggard.
